title: A read-only agent does not hold a task's work
summary: An agent declared read_only is never given a task's work: its work turn bound to a task is refused before any workspace is resolved, the operator cannot assign it a task, a run of it cannot claim one, and a flow does not select it for ordinary work. It stays a reviewer. Today such a turn runs in the operator's own checkout and nothing snapshots it (F425).
problem: worktrees.takes_task_workspace returns True only for a writing agent, so a read_only agent's task-bound turn resolves to the project directory -- the operator's checkout -- and, not being isolated, is never snapshotted. read_only drives no runner flag or sandbox, so the agent can still write. Nothing in the app sets read_only, but POST /agents/register and the agent config API do.

in_scope: The dispatch of a turn bound to a task's work (task_id, not review_task_id) for a read_only agent
The operator's task create and PATCH naming a read_only agent as assignee
An agent run's claim (-> in_progress) by a read_only agent
A flow's selection of an agent for ordinary work
non_goals: Review turns: a read_only agent reviewing in its detached review checkout is the intended use
Unassigning tasks that already name a read_only agent: they stay as they are, visible; their turns are refused with the remedy
Making read_only a sandbox: it stays a workspace declaration

requirements.statement: The system MUST refuse, before resolving any workspace, a turn for an agent declared read_only whose delivered input binds it to a task's work, naming the agent, the task and the remedy (assign a writing agent, or clear read_only), and leaving nothing staged.
requirements.rationale: The harm is the turn itself; this is the one chokepoint every assigning door leads to.

requirements.statement: The operator's task create and update MUST refuse to name an agent declared read_only as a task's assignee, and an agent run of such an agent MUST NOT claim a task.
requirements.rationale: Refused where the operator is looking, rather than later at a turn they did not start.

requirements.statement: A flow MUST NOT select an agent declared read_only for ordinary work, and MUST still consider it as a reviewer.
requirements.rationale: Otherwise the flow stages work its own dispatch then refuses, and stalls.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task assigned (grandfathered) to read_only agent 'reader'
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator triggers reader with that task
acceptance_criteria.then: 409 naming reader, the task and the remedy; no run, no workspace, nothing written to the project directory

acceptance_criteria.given: a completed task with evidence naming a commit
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator dispatches reader's review of it
acceptance_criteria.then: the review starts in reader's review checkout as today

acceptance_criteria.when: the operator creates a task with assignee reader, or PATCHes one to reader
acceptance_criteria.then: 422 naming reader as read-only; nothing created or changed

acceptance_criteria.when: a run of reader moves it to in_progress

acceptance_criteria.given: a flow whose roster has reader and writer free and one pending task and one completed task
acceptance_criteria.then: the pending task goes to writer, never reader; reader may be selected as the completed task's reviewer

acceptance_criteria.given: on the trial Hub, a read_only agent registered through the API and a task assigned to it before this change
acceptance_criteria.when: the operator triggers it on the task
acceptance_criteria.then: refused with the remedy and the project directory's git status unchanged; on the pre-fix Hub the turn runs in the project directory

tasks.title: Failing tests for the read-only boundary
One predicate, four doors
tasks.description: worktrees.is_writing_agent is the predicate. agent_trigger: refuse a work-bound turn for a non-writing agent ahead of the workspace (beside takes_task_workspace's use). tasks.py create/PATCH: refuse a read_only assignee. task_transition_service._guard_run_holds_the_task: refuse a read_only claimant. scheduler: exclude non-writing agents from the ordinary-work pool, not from resolve_reviewer.

tasks.title: Acceptance drive on :8010
tasks.description: scripts/drive/d1007_read_only_drive.py, failing on the pre-fix Hub.

design: Tier 1. The finding's suggestion was to refuse at assignment in one service function; reading the code, six places write an assignee (task create, PATCH, bind_run_to_task, enter_selected_task, the divergence escalation, the revision return) and only one place turns an assignment into writing -- the dispatch's workspace resolution. So the turn refusal is the guarantee and the assignment refusals are the early, legible feedback at the doors the operator and agents use. Tasks already assigned to a read_only agent are not rewritten (no migration); their turns are refused with the remedy. The divergence escalation and revision return name agents that already wrote, so they are not doors for this.

checked: worktrees.takes_task_workspace: task_id is not None and is_writing_agent(config) and is_git_repo(repo_root)
agent_trigger resolves the workspace via resolve_turn_workspace after takes_task_workspace (~1233-1275)
read_only is a key in the agent's config (worktrees.is_writing_agent), set only through the API
